# oq complete technical reference
> Query, edit and validate Org documents through one Rust engine.

## Compiled CLI contract
```text
oq — query, edit, and validate Org documents

Usage:
  oq query <jq-expression> <file.org>
  oq <jq-expression> <file.org>
  oq set [-i|--in-place] <jq-transformation> <file.org>
  oq validate --schema <schema.toml> <file.org>
  oq --help | oq -h
  oq --version

Options:
  -h, --help         Show this help; use as a standalone invocation.
  --version          Show the compiled version; use alone.
  -i, --in-place     For set only: update the input file atomically, with no stdout.
  --schema <path>    Required for validate: explicit TOML schema, with no default.

Output and defaults:
  query emits compact newline-separated JSON values, not an enclosing array.
  empty emits nothing; false and null emit JSON values. Each still exits 0.
  An array result is one JSON value; use .[] to emit its items.
  Without -i, set writes edited Org to stdout and leaves its input unchanged.
  validate writes one JSON report: {"mode":null,"diagnostics":[]} when valid.
  Each diagnostic has rule_id, severity (error/warning), line (1-based or null),
  and message. Warnings alone succeed; error diagnostics exit 1.
  Inputs and schemas are UTF-8 files. No command prompts for input.

Schemas:
  TOML requires version = 1. Add [[rules]] with id, assert (a jq predicate),
  and message; select defaults to ".", severity to "error", min_matches to 0.
  Use min_matches = 1 when an empty selection must fail. Assertions must emit
  exactly one boolean. Optional [[modes]] choose the first matching mode.

Environment:
  No oq-specific runtime environment variables or ambient configuration files.
  Files and schemas come only from explicit arguments; no schema autodiscovery.
  Build/install tools have their own environment; this describes the oq CLI.

Safety:
  set accepts supported scalar edits and new properties, not arbitrary tree edits.
  Invalid edits leave the input unchanged. In-place edits preserve permissions
  and require a writable regular file; symlinks are rejected.
  Expressions have no shell/process or external-module file loader. env, now,
  debug, stderr, and halt_error are unavailable; halt returns an error.
  Expressions can consume CPU/memory; this is not an untrusted-code sandbox.

Exit codes:
  0  Success, including empty/false/null query results and warning-only validation.
  1  Document validation has at least one error diagnostic (JSON on stdout).
  2  Usage, I/O, expression/edit, malformed schema, or schema-evaluation error.
    Error text is written to stderr.

Runnable schema examples and complete library reference: repository llms-full.txt.
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-h, --help` | Show this help; use as a standalone invocation. |
| `--version` | Show the compiled version; use alone. |
| `-i, --in-place` | For set only: update the input file atomically, with no stdout. |
| `--schema <path>` | Required for validate: explicit TOML schema, with no default. |

## Runnable validation workflow
Run these blocks in order in an empty directory with `oq` on `PATH`.

<!-- oq:case:valid -->

```sh
cat > note.org <<'ORG'
* Note
:PROPERTIES:
:state: ready
:END:
ORG
cat > strict.toml <<'TOML'
version = 1
[[rules]]
id = "note.state"
select = ".children[]"
assert = '.properties.state == "ready"'
message = "State must be ready"
line = ".property_lines.state // .line"
min_matches = 1
TOML
oq validate --schema strict.toml note.org
```

Exit 0: JSON report with no diagnostics. The rule requires a note in state `ready`.

<!-- oq:case:rejected -->

```sh
oq set -i '.children[0].properties.state = "blocked"' note.org
oq validate --schema strict.toml note.org
```

Exit 1: JSON error `note.state` at line 3. The in-place edit itself is silent.

<!-- oq:case:warning -->

```sh
cp strict.toml warning.toml
printf '\nseverity = "warning"\n' >> warning.toml
oq validate --schema warning.toml note.org
```

Exit 0: the same violation is a warning diagnostic, not an error.

<!-- oq:case:malformed -->

```sh
printf 'version = [\n' > broken.toml
oq validate --schema broken.toml note.org
```

Exit 2: malformed schema; error text on stderr.

<!-- oq:case:usage -->

```sh
oq validate note.org
```

Exit 2: `--schema` is required even if a schema file exists nearby.

## Automation and security
Commands never prompt. Parse query output as a JSON stream, not one enclosing
array; a query returning an array emits that array as a single line. Use the
exit status as documented above: false/null are data, not failures.

Validation reports contain mode and diagnostics. Each diagnostic contains a
schema-defined rule_id/message, severity, and a 1-based line or null. A schema
with only version=1 is valid but has no checks; use real rules and min_matches
when selection is required. Schema syntax/evaluation failures exit 2, distinct
from document rejection at exit 1.

The CLI reads its named UTF-8 input/schema files. There is no oq environment
configuration, schema search, network service, shell execution, or module file
loader. The OS still supplies normal process startup/PATH. Build/publish tooling
has separate configuration described in the contributor guide. In-place edits
write only the named regular file after validation, via a same-directory atomic
replacement, retaining permissions and rejecting symlinks/read-only files.
Treat jq predicates as caller-supplied code: CPU/memory use is not sandboxed.

## Libraries and architecture
oq-core provides parse(source), query(source, expression), set(source, expression),
validate(source, schema_toml), and Schema::from_toml(schema_toml). Fallible Rust
operations return Result, never terminate the host process, and do not perform
CLI filesystem I/O. The CLI adapts these APIs to files and exit codes.

The @agent-harbor/oq package exports async createOq(bytes_or_module). Await it to
get parse, query, set and validate methods. It executes the same Rust core through
WebAssembly, with no global CLI dependency or duplicate JavaScript parser. The
typed wrapper owns and frees buffers and turns structured errors into exceptions.
The detailed model/schema/ABI contract follows, derived from its canonical page.

# Document, query, mutation, and schema contract

The Rust library, command-line application, and JavaScript bindings share one
engine. Org syntax is recognized by [orgize](https://github.com/PoiScript/orgize)
and jq expressions by [jaq](https://github.com/01mf02/jaq). They are not inferred
from file extensions or application-specific property names.

## Parsed document

`parse(source)` returns a JSON-compatible document. `children` contains all
top-level headings in source order; each heading has `children` recursively.
`sections` is a lookup of top-level headings by exact title; when titles
repeat it addresses the first, while `children` retains every occurrence.
The two views refer to the same source locations. Every heading exposes:

- `title`, read-only `title_plain`, `level`, `line` (one-based), `start`, `end`
  (UTF-8 byte offsets);
- `properties` (lowercase keys and string values), `property_lines`,
  `property_order`, and `drawer_stray_lines`;
- `content`: direct body lines with `text` and `line`, excluding the property
  drawer and descendant headings;
- `items`: list items, including nested items, with `text`, read-only `text_plain`, `checkbox`
  (`" "`, `"X"`, `"-"`, or null), `line`, `indent`, `fields` and `field_lines`;
- `tables`: arrays of rows, each with `cells` and `line`; rule rows are omitted.
  Empty leading, middle, trailing, and whitespace-only cells retain their column
  positions. A final closing pipe adds no extra column; a row may omit it.
- `paragraphs`: read-only direct prose records with raw `text`, rendered `plain`,
  one-based `line`, and half-open UTF-8 byte `start`/`end` offsets. Records retain
  source whitespace, physical newlines, and indentation, including the prose's
  final newline when present. Separating blank lines and affiliated keywords are
  excluded. Drawers, tables, blocks, list-owned prose, and descendant headings
  do not contribute direct prose records.

The document also exposes `title`, `title_line`, `keywords` (key/value/line),
`content`, `items`, `tables`, and `paragraphs` for the preamble. Valid literal blocks keep
their contents opaque. As the [Org manual](https://orgmode.org/manual/Literal-Examples.html)
requires, comma-quote heading-like and keyword-like example lines (`,*` and
`,#+`). An unescaped column-zero `*` remains a heading even inside a block;
`oq` delegates that grammar to orgize. Nested headings retain their
actual levels. Parsing is tolerant: malformed drawers remain observable for
schema diagnostics instead of being silently repaired.

`fields` interprets a list item's first `name: value` line and its aligned
continuation fields as a description record. Continuation text is retained,
including multiline values. This is an optional structured view over Org list
items, not a YAML parser. Native `term :: definition` items also expose fields.

Completed checkboxes accept both `[x]` and `[X]` and expose the normalized state
`"X"`. Untargeted edits and no-op transformations preserve the original case;
the writable states remain `" "`, `"X"`, and `"-"`.

The additive display projections leave every raw field and its mutation span
unchanged. `title_plain` renders the trimmed heading title. Item `text_plain`
renders only paragraphs owned by that item, excluding bullet, checkbox,
description-tag syntax, and child lists. Only the whole item's outer edges are
trimmed. A paragraph's terminal LF/CRLF is replaced as needed to join separate
paragraphs with one normalized `\n\n` separator. Other source whitespace,
including physical newlines inside paragraphs, trailing spaces, and indentation
of later paragraphs, is retained.

Rendering follows orgize's inline nodes: balanced bold, italic, underline,
strike-through, code, and verbatim delimiters are removed, recursively rendering
their content. Links render their label, or their complete target when no label
is present (including `file:`). Unmatched markup remains literal. Rendering never
matches markup across paragraphs or headings, and literal blocks remain opaque.
For example, `* Deploy =tool= with *care*` has raw title
`Deploy =tool= with *care*` and `title_plain` `Deploy tool with care`.
`- [x] Read [[file:guide.org][the /guide/]] and [[file:other.org]]` has
`text_plain` `Read the guide and file:other.org`, while its raw `text` retains
the link and emphasis syntax.

For example, the body below has two paragraph records:

```org
* Note
  First /line/,
  then =code=.

  Another paragraph.
```

Their `plain` values are `"  First line,\n  then code.\n"` and
`"  Another paragraph.\n"` when the source uses LF line endings and ends with
a newline. Their `text` and byte spans retain the original markup and spacing.

## Queries and edits

Recursive jq traversal (`..`) visits both root views. Select through `children`
when a rule should visit each source heading once, for example
`.children[] | recurse(.children[]?)`. A selector's emitted values determine its
diagnostics; the engine does not silently deduplicate equal values.

`query(source, expression)` returns every JSON value emitted by the jq program.
It supports jaq's standard JSON operators and pure functions, plus jq's `IN`
stream-membership helper. Environment/clock functions (`env`, `now`) and logging
or process-oriented helpers (`debug`, `stderr`, `halt_error`) are deliberately
unavailable in both native and WASM execution. Modules cannot load external
files. `halt` returns an evaluation error instead of terminating its host.
Invalid programs fail explicitly. Sources are limited to 32 MiB; query
streams are limited to 100,000 outputs per call.
For example:

```sh
oq query '.sections["Work"].children[] | select(.properties.state == "active")' work.org
oq query '[.. | objects | select(has("checkbox")) | .text]' work.org
oq set -i '.sections.Work.children[0].properties.state = "done"' work.org
```

`set` evaluates a jq transformation of the parsed document. It must return
exactly one document with the original structure. Writable scalars are the
document title, heading titles, existing property values, item text and checkbox
states, description-record values, and table cells. New properties may be added
to a heading's `properties` map; a missing drawer is inserted after the heading
and its optional Org planning line, using the local newline style. Other keys, arrays,
metadata, and deletions are read-only. Unsupported edits fail before any file
write. Strings containing line breaks, structural delimiters, or values that
change the parsed structure are rejected. Multiline description fields are
queryable; mutation of a multiline field is rejected to avoid discarding layout.
Direct edits to `title_plain`, `text_plain`, or `paragraphs` are rejected. Edit
the existing canonical raw scalars instead; reparsing recomputes the projections.

Edits replace only the selected scalar's byte span. Untargeted bytes, spacing,
line endings, and the final newline are preserved. Changes through duplicate
views of the same span must agree. Conflicting or overlapping edits fail.
Mutating several independent scalars in one expression is supported. Reparse
checks prevent an edit from changing the document's structural shape.

The CLI writes through a same-directory temporary file and atomic rename,
preserving file permissions. Symlinks are rejected for in-place updates rather
than replacing their directory entries. Document validation error diagnostics
use exit 1 and a JSON report on stdout. Warnings alone and successful commands
use exit 0. Usage, I/O, expression/edit, malformed-schema and schema evaluation
errors use exit 2 and error text on stderr. CLI `query` emits newline-separated
JSON values; CLI `validate` emits one JSON report. To inspect a parsed document
through the CLI, use `oq query '.' file.org`. `parse(source)` is a library API.

## Declarative schemas

Schemas are TOML documents with `version = 1`, ordered `[[modes]]`, and
`[[rules]]`. Unknown fields, duplicate names/ids, invalid jq programs, unknown
modes, and invalid types are errors, including rules in inactive modes. Regexes
are evaluated by jq's `test`/`match` functions; an invalid dynamically supplied
pattern is an evaluation error, never a successful assertion.
No application grammar is compiled into the engine.

```toml
version = 1

[[modes]]
name = "single"
when = '.children | length == 1'

[[modes]]
name = "multiple"
when = 'true'

[[rules]]
id = "entry.scope"
select = '.children[]'
assert = '.properties.scope | IN("global", "project", "repository")'
message = "Invalid or missing scope"
line = '.property_lines.scope // .line'
severity = "error"

[[rules]]
id = "entry.project"
select = '.children[] | select(.properties.scope == "project")'
assert = '(.properties.project // "") | length > 0'
message = "Project scope requires a project"

[[rules]]
id = "entry.refs"
select = '.children[]'
assert = '(.properties.refs // "") | test("^\\S+(,\\s*\\S+)*$")'
message = "References must be a nonempty coordinate list"

[[rules]]
id = "entry.body"
select = '.children[]'
assert = '[.content[] | select(.text | test("\\S"))] | length <= 12'
message = "Body exceeds twelve nonempty lines"

[[rules]]
id = "entry.body.warning"
select = '.children[]'
assert = '[.content[] | select(.text | test("\\S"))] | length <= 6'
message = "Prefer six body lines"
severity = "warning"
```

Each mode's `when` runs against the complete document and must return exactly
one boolean. The first matching mode wins; no match is a diagnostic. With no
modes the mode is null. A rule's optional `modes` list limits its applicability.
The default selector is `.`. The assertion must return exactly one boolean;
zero outputs is an error, never an accidental pass. Each false result produces
one diagnostic. Optional `min_matches` rejects an empty or undersized selection.

`message` is literal; optional `message_query` instead computes exactly one
string against the selected node, allowing exact contextual diagnostics.
`line` computes one positive integer or null (default `.line // null`).
Diagnostics preserve rule order and selection order, with `rule_id`, `severity`,
`line`, and `message`. Schema and evaluation errors are returned separately from
document validation failures.

The same primitives express title suffixes (`endswith`), required/allowed and
prohibited sections (`has`, `keys`, `all`, `startswith`), drawer key sets,
enums (`IN`), patterns (`test`), conditional required properties (`if`), direct
child requirements, subsection prefixes, description-record fields, table
columns, and body limits. File modes are schema data. An overlay replaces the
schema input; it requires no Rust rebuild.

## Library and WebAssembly

`oq_core::{parse, query, set, validate, Schema}` accept source strings; all
fallible operations return `Result`. Filesystem writes belong to the CLI only.
No library operation exits the process or reads ambient configuration.

The WASM boundary passes UTF-8 JSON requests to the same Rust functions.
`oq_alloc(length)` returns an owned zeroed buffer, `oq_execute(ptr,length)`
borrows it and returns a separate response allocation encoded as
`(pointer << 32) | length`, and `oq_free(ptr,length)` releases exactly one
allocation. The caller must pass only live allocated ranges. The TypeScript
wrapper owns both allocations, refreshes memory views after calls, frees in
`finally`, and translates structured errors into exceptions. There is no shared
result buffer or global state. WebAssembly modules are instantiated without
imports, and the Node tests exercise the compiled module directly.
